mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic concerns rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% over a 3-month period, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in the same period, signals strong consumer demand and a robust labor market, typically leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both trigger conditions are met, or if the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period, coupled with a stable or decreasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), signals disinflationary pressure without monetary tightening, typically leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS stable or decreases in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both trigger conditions are met, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over a 3-month period, with no significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strengthening labor market without over-heating, typically leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 1% and UNRATE stable in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both trigger conditions are met, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 increases, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
